name: shortcut-menu-bar
description: Add handy buttons like beautify, show opened files, save, toggle terminal, activity bar etc to editor menu bar. User-defined buttons are also possible.

ShortcutMenuBar.buttonOrder.title: button order
ShortcutMenuBar.buttonOrder.markdownDescription: order of the buttons in the editor title bar, left to right. Buttons listed here come first, everything left out keeps its usual place after them; an empty list means the default order. Buttons that are turned off take no space, so the list can name them anyway. _The order is relative to the buttons of this extension only — other extensions place their own buttons in the same title bar and are not affected. Applied to the extension manifest, so a window reload is needed and only the User setting is used, not a workspace one_

ShortcutMenuBar.buttonWhen.markdownDescription: extra condition for showing a button, so that it only appears where it is of use. Keys are button ids, values are [when clauses](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/when-clause-contexts) — the same expressions keyboard shortcuts use, e.g. `editorLangId == python` or `resourceExtname == .md`. The condition is added to the one the button already has, so it never brings back a button that is switched off or, for a user button, has no command. Remove a key to show that button everywhere again. _Run `Developer: Inspect Context Keys` to see what holds true where you are pointing. Applied to the extension manifest, so a window reload is needed and only the User setting is used, not a workspace one_

ShortcutMenuBar.userButton01Command.title: command
ShortcutMenuBar.userButton01Command.markdownDescription: command executed with 'user action 1'; _icon is shown if set_

ShortcutMenuBar.userButton01Title.title: title
ShortcutMenuBar.userButton01Title.markdownDescription: tooltip shown when hovering the 'user action 1' button; _defaults to 'user action 1'. Applied to the extension manifest, so a window reload is needed and only the User setting is used, not a workspace one_

ShortcutMenuBar.userButton01Icon.title: icon
ShortcutMenuBar.userButton01Icon.markdownDescription: icon of the 'user action 1' button. Either a built-in icon written as `$(rocket)` — **[browse all built-in icons](https://microsoft.github.io/vscode-codicons/dist/codicon.html)**, hover an icon there to get its id — or an image file: a path of your own (`~` and `${userHome}` are expanded), or `extension:publisher.name/path/icon.svg` to borrow one from another installed extension. For light themes add a second file after a `|` (`dark|light`); given just one, a sibling file suffixed with `_light` is used when there is one. _Leave empty for the default numbered icon. Applied to the extension manifest, so a window reload is needed and only the User setting is used, not a workspace one_
